test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 22 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which Amendment of the Citizenship Act introduced the provision that an illegal migrant cannot acquire citizenship by naturalisation or registration?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2003 Amendment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **2003 Amendment** to the Citizenship Act introduced provisions restricting illegal migrants from acquiring Indian citizenship through registration or naturalisation.
 
• An illegal migrant is defined as a person who enters India without valid travel documents or stays beyond the permitted time frame.
 
• The amendment was brought during the tenure of the Atal Bihari Vajpayee-led NDA government.
 
• This amendment also laid the groundwork for the creation of the **National Register of Citizens (NRC)**, aimed at identifying illegal migrants in India.
 
• The Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2003, added Section 14A, mandating the government to issue a national identity card and maintain the NRC.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Illegal Migrant Definition:**

 
 
• An illegal migrant is a foreign national who enters India without valid documentation (e.g., passport, visa).
 
• Staying in India beyond the permitted duration also qualifies as illegal migration.
 
 
 
• **National Register of Citizens (NRC):**
 
 
• The NRC was first created in Assam to identify illegal migrants, specifically those who entered after March 24, 1971.
 
• The 2003 Amendment paved the way for its potential nationwide implementation.
 
 
 
• **Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019:**
 
 
• It amended the Citizenship Act, 1955, allowing certain persecuted minorities from Pakistan, Bangladesh, and Afghanistan to acquire Indian citizenship.
 
• Excludes illegal migrants who are not part of the specified religious communities.
 
 
 
• **Modes of Acquiring Citizenship in India:**
 
 
• By birth.
 
• By descent.
 
• By registration.
 
• By naturalisation.
 
• By incorporation of territory.
